theory.intro: A **composite solid** is built from simpler solids joined together, such as a barn made of a rectangular prism with a half-cylinder roof. Find the volume of each part, then combine them.
facts: Prism $V = Ah$ (a box is $V = lwh$), cylinder $V = \pi r^{2}h$, half-cylinder $V = \frac{1}{2}\pi r^{2}h$.
A cylinder's formula uses the **radius**; when a diameter is given, halve it first.
Keep the working exact and round only at the last line.
Capacity uses $1$ m³ $= 1000$ L and $1000$ cm³ $= 1$ L.
All lengths must be in the same unit before the volumes are combined.
steps: Split the composite solid into simple prisms and cylinders.
Find the volume of each simple solid.
Add the volumes, or subtract any that are holes.

foundation.solution_text:
Split the solid into a rectangular prism and a half-cylinder (roof radius $r = 3$ m).
$V_{\text{box}} = lwh$
$= 6 \times 4 \times 10$
$= 240\text{ m}^{3}$
$V_{\text{roof}} = \frac{1}{2}\pi r^{2}h$
$= \frac{1}{2} \times \pi \times 3^{2} \times 10$
$= 141.3716\ldots\text{ m}^{3}$
$V = 240 + 141.3716\ldots$
$= 381.3716\ldots$
$\approx 381.4\text{ m}^{3}$

Split the solid into the rectangular prism base and the cylinder.
$V_{\text{base}} = lwh$
$= 8 \times 8 \times 3$
$= 192\text{ m}^{3}$
$V_{\text{cyl}} = \pi r^{2}h$
$= \pi \times 2^{2} \times 6$
$= 75.3982\ldots\text{ m}^{3}$
$V = 192 + 75.3982\ldots$
$= 267.3982\ldots$
$\approx 267.4\text{ m}^{3}$

Take the volume of the block and subtract the cylindrical hole (radius $2$ cm, depth $5$ cm).
$V_{\text{block}} = lwh$
$= 10 \times 6 \times 5$
$= 300\text{ cm}^{3}$
$V_{\text{hole}} = \pi r^{2}h$
$= \pi \times 2^{2} \times 5$
$= 62.8318\ldots\text{ cm}^{3}$
$V = 300 - 62.8318\ldots$
$= 237.1681\ldots$
$\approx 237.2\text{ cm}^{3}$

Split the solid into the two cylinders and add their volumes.
$V_{\text{lower}} = \pi r^{2}h$
$= \pi \times 5^{2} \times 3$
$= 235.6194\ldots\text{ cm}^{3}$
$V_{\text{upper}} = \pi r^{2}h$
$= \pi \times 2^{2} \times 6$
$= 75.3982\ldots\text{ cm}^{3}$
$V = 235.6194\ldots + 75.3982\ldots$
$= 311.0176\ldots$
$\approx 311.0\text{ cm}^{3}$

Take the outer cylinder and subtract the inner cylinder (the hollow middle).
$V_{\text{outer}} = \pi r^{2}h$
$= \pi \times 4^{2} \times 20$
$= 1005.3096\ldots\text{ cm}^{3}$
$V_{\text{inner}} = \pi r^{2}h$
$= \pi \times 3^{2} \times 20$
$= 565.4866\ldots\text{ cm}^{3}$
$V = 1005.3096\ldots - 565.4866\ldots$
$= 439.8229\ldots$
$\approx 439.8\text{ cm}^{3}$

Split the bolt into the square-prism head and the cylindrical shaft.
$V_{\text{head}} = lwh$
$= 4 \times 4 \times 2$
$= 32\text{ mm}^{3}$
$V_{\text{shaft}} = \pi r^{2}h$
$= \pi \times 1.5^{2} \times 8$
$= 56.5486\ldots\text{ mm}^{3}$
$V = 32 + 56.5486\ldots$
$= 88.5486\ldots$
$\approx 88.5\text{ mm}^{3}$

Split the solid into the block and the cylinder.
$V_{\text{block}} = lwh$
$= 2 \times 2 \times 0.5$
$= 2\text{ m}^{3}$
$V_{\text{cyl}} = \pi r^{2}h$
$= \pi \times 0.6^{2} \times 2$
$= 2.2619\ldots\text{ m}^{3}$
$V = 2 + 2.2619\ldots$
$= 4.2619\ldots\text{ m}^{3}$
Total volume in litres $= 4.2619\ldots \times 1000$
$= 4261.9\text{ L}$

foundation.question_text:
A hollow pipe has an outside radius of $5\text{ cm}$, an inside radius of $3\text{ cm}$ and a length of $18\text{ cm}$.
Find the volume of the pipe material, in $\text{cm}^{3}$, correct to $1$ decimal place.
foundation.solution_text:
Take the outer cylinder and subtract the inner cylinder.
$V_{\text{outer}} = \pi r^{2}h$
$= \pi \times 5^{2} \times 18$
$= 450\pi\text{ cm}^{3}$
$V_{\text{inner}} = \pi r^{2}h$
$= \pi \times 3^{2} \times 18$
$= 162\pi\text{ cm}^{3}$
$V = 450\pi - 162\pi$
$= 288\pi$
$= 904.7786\ldots$
$\approx 904.8\text{ cm}^{3}$

development.question_text: A grain silo is a cylinder of radius $2$ m and height $8$ m standing on a square concrete slab of side $6$ m and thickness $0.5$ m. Find the total volume of the structure, in m³, correct to $1$ decimal place.
development.solution_text:
Split the structure into the cylinder and the square slab.
$V_{\text{cyl}} = \pi r^{2}h$
$= \pi \times 2^{2} \times 8$
$= 100.5309\ldots\text{ m}^{3}$
$V_{\text{slab}} = lwh$
$= 6 \times 6 \times 0.5$
$= 18\text{ m}^{3}$
$V = 100.5309\ldots + 18$
$= 118.5309\ldots$
$\approx 118.5\text{ m}^{3}$

Take the block and subtract both cylindrical holes (each radius $1.5$ cm, depth $4$ cm).
$V_{\text{block}} = lwh$
$= 12 \times 8 \times 4$
$= 384\text{ cm}^{3}$
$V_{\text{holes}} = 2 \times \pi r^{2}h$
$= 2 \times \pi \times 1.5^{2} \times 4$
$= 56.5486\ldots\text{ cm}^{3}$
$V = 384 - 56.5486\ldots$
$= 327.4513\ldots$
$\approx 327.5\text{ cm}^{3}$

development.question_text:
A cylinder of radius $4\text{ cm}$ and height $10\text{ cm}$ sits on a cube of edge $8\text{ cm}$.
Find the total volume of the composite solid, in $\text{cm}^{3}$, correct to $1$ decimal place.
development.solution_text:
Split the solid into the cube and the cylinder.
$V_{\text{cube}} = l^{3}$
$= 8^{3}$
$= 512\text{ cm}^{3}$
$V_{\text{cyl}} = \pi r^{2}h$
$= \pi \times 4^{2} \times 10$
$= 502.6548\ldots\text{ cm}^{3}$
$V = 512 + 502.6548\ldots$
$= 1014.6548\ldots$
$\approx 1014.7\text{ cm}^{3}$

development.question_text:
A cylinder of radius $2\text{ cm}$ and height $5\text{ cm}$ stands on a cube of edge $6\text{ cm}$.
Find the total volume of the composite solid, in $\text{cm}^{3}$, correct to $1$ decimal place.
development.solution_text:
Split the solid into the cube and the cylinder.
$V_{\text{cube}} = l^{3}$
$= 6^{3}$
$= 216\text{ cm}^{3}$
$V_{\text{cyl}} = \pi r^{2}h$
$= \pi \times 2^{2} \times 5$
$= 62.8318\ldots\text{ cm}^{3}$
$V = 216 + 62.8318\ldots$
$= 278.8318\ldots$
$\approx 278.8\text{ cm}^{3}$

development.question_text:
A block is a $9\text{ cm}$ by $5\text{ cm}$ by $6\text{ cm}$ rectangular prism with a cylindrical hole of radius $2\text{ cm}$ drilled through the $6\text{ cm}$ depth.
Find the volume of material remaining, in $\text{cm}^{3}$, correct to $1$ decimal place.
development.solution_text:
Subtract the cylindrical hole from the block.
$V_{\text{block}} = 9 \times 5 \times 6$
$= 270\text{ cm}^{3}$
$V_{\text{hole}} = \pi \times 2^{2} \times 6$
$= 75.3982\ldots\text{ cm}^{3}$
$V = 270 - 75.3982\ldots$
$= 194.6017\ldots$
$\approx 194.6\text{ cm}^{3}$

Split the shed into a rectangular prism and a half-cylinder (roof radius $r = 4$ m).
$V_{\text{box}} = lwh$
$= 8 \times 5 \times 15$
$= 600\text{ m}^{3}$
$V_{\text{roof}} = \frac{1}{2}\pi r^{2}h$
$= \frac{1}{2} \times \pi \times 4^{2} \times 15$
$= 376.9911\ldots\text{ m}^{3}$
$V = 600 + 376.9911\ldots$
$= 976.9911\ldots$
$\approx 977.0\text{ m}^{3}$

mastery.question_text:
A concrete support column is a square prism standing on a cylindrical base.
The cylindrical base is $1\text{ m}$ in diameter and $1\text{ m}$ high.
The square prism is $10\text{ m}$ long and its square cross-section has area $0.5\text{ m}^{2}$.
Show that the total volume is approximately $5.8\text{ m}^{3}$, correct to $1$ decimal place.
mastery.solution_text:
Split the column into the cylindrical base and the square prism.
$V_{\text{cyl}} = \pi r^{2}h$
$= \pi \times 0.5^{2} \times 1$
$= 0.25\pi\text{ m}^{3}$
$V_{\text{prism}} = Ah$
$= \frac{1}{2} \times 10$
$= 5\text{ m}^{3}$
$V = 0.25\pi + 5$
$= 5.7853\ldots$
$\approx 5.8\text{ m}^{3}$

mastery.question_text:
A tank is a cylinder of radius $1$ m and height $2$ m sitting on top of a rectangular prism $2$ m by $2$ m by $1$ m, and the whole tank holds water.
Water flows in at $200$ litres per minute.
Using $1$ m³ $= 1000$ L, find how long it takes to fill the tank, in minutes, correct to $1$ decimal place.
mastery.solution_text:
$V_{\text{prism}} = lwh$
$= 2 \times 2 \times 1$
$= 4\text{ m}^{3}$
$V_{\text{cyl}} = \pi r^{2}h$
$= \pi \times 1^{2} \times 2$
$= 6.2831\ldots\text{ m}^{3}$
$V = 4 + 6.2831\ldots$
$= 10.2831\ldots\text{ m}^{3}$
Capacity $= 10.2831\ldots \times 1000$
$= 10283.1\ldots\text{ L}$
Time $= \frac{10283.1\ldots}{200}$
$= 51.4159\ldots$
$\approx 51.4\text{ minutes}$

mastery.question_text:
A tunnel is $12\text{ m}$ long and has a semicircular opening $6\text{ m}$ wide.
Its concrete shell is $1\text{ m}$ thick, so the outside radius is $4\text{ m}$.
Find the volume of concrete needed, in $\text{m}^{3}$, correct to $3$ decimal places.
mastery.solution_text:
Subtract the inner half-cylinder from the outer half-cylinder.
The inside radius is $3\text{ m}$.
$V_{\text{outer}} = \frac{1}{2}\pi r^{2}h$
$= \frac{1}{2} \times \pi \times 4^{2} \times 12$
$= 96\pi\text{ m}^{3}$
$V_{\text{inner}} = \frac{1}{2}\pi r^{2}h$
$= \frac{1}{2} \times \pi \times 3^{2} \times 12$
$= 54\pi\text{ m}^{3}$
$V = 96\pi - 54\pi$
$= 42\pi$
$= 131.946891\ldots$
$\approx 131.947\text{ m}^{3}$
